source: NCERT Class IX, Contemporary India I, Geography Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. Location and Extent
points: India lies **entirely in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres**.
**Latitudinal extent:** **8°4′ N to 37°6′ N**; **Longitudinal extent:** **68°7′ E to 97°25′ E**.
The **Tropic of Cancer (23°30′ N)** passes through the **middle** of India (through 8 states).
India is the **seventh largest** country in the world; area ≈ **3.28 million sq km** (~**2.4%** of the world's land area).

sections.heading: 2. Standard Meridian and Time
points: The **Standard Meridian of India = 82°30′ E**, passing through **Mirzapur (Uttar Pradesh)**.
**Indian Standard Time (IST)** is based on it and is **5 hours 30 minutes ahead of GMT**.
Though the country spans ~30° of longitude (about **2 hours** of sun-time between Gujarat and Arunachal), one standard time is used for the whole country.

sections.heading: 3. India and the World — Neighbours
points: India's landmass has a central location between **East and West Asia**; the **Indian Ocean** (named after India) lies to the south.

sub: **Pakistan and Afghanistan** (NW), **China, Nepal, Bhutan** (N), **Myanmar and Bangladesh** (E).

points: **Sri Lanka** and **Maldives** are island neighbours to the south (separated by the **Gulf of Mannar** and **Palk Strait**).
The **Suez Canal (1869)** shortened India's distance to Europe.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Latitude 8°4′N–37°6′N; longitude 68°7′E–97°25′E; entirely in N & E hemispheres.
Tropic of Cancer (23°30′N) passes through the middle of India.
India = 7th largest country; ~3.28 million sq km (~2.4% of world land).
Neighbours: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh; islands: Sri Lanka, Maldives.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Tropic of Cancer (23°30′ N)** divides India roughly into north and south.
India is the **7th largest** country by area.
**Sri Lanka** is separated from India by the **Palk Strait** and **Gulf of Mannar**.
